newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares mixed, gains not seen soon.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares mixed, gains not seen soon.

text.p: * Lithuanian share prices were mixed on Tuesday and dealers were not bullish about the bourse's immediate prospects.
* Overall market volume was around 10.3 million litas.
* Central market volume was only 850,000 litas while the secondary T-bill market turned over almost 5.6 million litas.
* The official list index fell 0.06 points to 943.00.
* The Litin A index edged up 3.01 points to 2,422.48, while the Litin G index rose 9.88 points to 2,137.32.
* Siauliu Bank rose ten percent for the second straight day, to 84.70 litas from 77.00 litas, but none of its shares swapped hands.
Lithuanian shares were mixed on Tuesday and dealers said they expected prices to ease more this week.
"The general trend right now is down...investors seem to be holding off and waiting for prices to fall some more," said Sigitas Petraitis of brokerage house Vilfima.
Dealers also said that some big shareholders appeared to want to cut their losses by bailing out, pushing the supply of shares up and prices down.
Siauliu Bank rose ten percent for the second straight session, to 84.70 litas from 77.00 litas, but none of its shares changed hands.
Dealers said the market was responding to Hermis Bank's intention to acquire a majority stake in the small regional bank.
Despite the slight increase in the index, the session saw more losers than gainers.
They included Rokishkis Cheese, which eased to 46.00 litas from 46.90 litas in trade of almost 35,000 litas.
Refrigerator maker Snaige eased slightly to 9.95 litas from 9.98 litas in light trade of only 597.00 litas but dealers were upbeat about its prospects.
"Snaige is a good company and it has room to move up," said one dealer.
The company earlier announced that its first quarter loss was 4.2 million litas
But is also said that it planned a 40 million litas share issue and that it was in talks with an unnamed western investor.
The secondary T-bill market was relatively active, turning over almost 5.6 million litas.
Dealers said one or two banks faced a bit of a liquidity crunch and that Tuesday's turnover was a not a sign that the once active market was picking up steam.
-- Ed Stoddard, Riga newsroom +370 2 22 35 18
